steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C). Grease a baking sheet with cooking spray or line with parchment paper.
Whisk together egg white and water in a medium bowl until frothy. Set aside.
Mix together sugar, salt, and cinnamon in a separate bowl.
Add pecans to egg white mixture; stir well to coat.
Transfer pecans to sugar mixture; toss to coat.
Spread pecans out evenly on the prepared baking sheet, being careful not to over crowd.
Bake in the preheated oven until crisp, stirring every 15 minutes, for about 1 hour. Let cool and enjoy.

raw_recipe.headline: Sugar-Coated Pecans
raw_recipe.description: These sugar-coated pecans are coated in egg white and cinnamon sugar, then slow-roasted until crunchy for a wonderfully sweet candied snack.

review.reviewBody: I would like to update my review. I have made these numerous times and they are well received. I have continued to use the two egg whites although I am not sure if it is necessary or not. I use 2 tsp. of water and 1 teaspoon of vanilla. They turn out wonderful. This is an outstanding recipe. I do make a slight change in the directions. I whip my egg whites in my 5 quart bowl from my Kitchen Aid Mixer. I add the pecans and stir. I then slowly add the sugar mixture right into the bowl with the pecans. I mix after each small addition of sugar. I find it mixes well this way. I have tried the ziploc bag method and find it is not necessary. All in one bowl works well for me. Another update as of 10/2009. I have continued to make these for parties and gifts. I get many requests for the recipe. In the past I always used sugar made from sugar beets. Recently I switched to buying sugar made from sugar cane. I have to say I prefer these made with sugar from sugar beets. It seems like the sugar from sugar cane melts more so the pecans look a bit different. They still taste okay, but I will be buying sugar from sugar beets again for this recipe.

Great recipe for holiday snacking. Definitely use 2 gallon-size ziploc bags with this recipe: Put the egg mixture in 1 bag and the sugar mixture in the other. Add the pecans to the first bag to coat, then transfer them to the 2nd bag and shake. Much easier to thoroughly coat the pecans!

I'm so impressed with this recipe that I went out and bought 5 pounds of whole pecans (at over $9.00 per pound!)and plan to put them in the 20+ baskets I give out at Christmas along with cookies, jams, and my famous lemon bread. Does anyone know how long they will last? Can they be frozen? Thanks! ** An update....the original recipe is the best for the most part...I tried it with vanilla...better with water.....also tried with brown sugar.....white is better. Two things I did do....used 2 egg whites and almost twice as much cinnamon. I got so many requests for the recipe. I will include these nuts in my baskets every year from now on. Easy and soooo tasty! Oh, and the kitchen smells wonderful while they are baking too...BTW, they freeze beautifully!

Delicious -- a big hit by all!! And so easy (especially when using 2 large Ziploc bags for coating nuts with egg white mixture; then another bag for the cinnamon sugar mixture; I used 1/2 granulated sugar and 1/2 dark brown sugar)!! A keeper!

I've been making these pecans for over 30 years. Not even sure where I got the recipe. Very easy to double. I buy the 2 lb bags of pecans at Costco, I think they are better than Sam's and much cheaper than the grocery store too. Between Thanksgiving and Christmas I go through at least 6 bags (12 + lbs). They make great gifts. I took a large tin to work and I found one of the guys at his desk with the entire tin. The only thing I modify is after I empty the bag in the bowl of egg white mixture until well moistened, about 5 minutes. This helps create a crispy pecan. During that time, prepare the sugar mixture and butter the pans. I stir the sugar mixture into the pecans until there isn't any loose sugar and divide them into 2 well buttered (not margarine or spray butter) cookie sheets (1 lb in each). Bake them at 250 for an hour stirring every 15 minutes. Very important to scrape the pans when stirring. As soon as they finish baking, remove them from the pans and cool on waxed paper. If you are bringing them to work or large gatherings, be prepared to provide the recipe or take orders.

These were simple to make and came out simply delicious.. A family favorite each year. I followed the directions almost exact however I used 1tsp of cinnamon 3/4tsp of nutmeg and a dash of vanilla in the egg white/water mixture. I put 2 slabs of butter on the baking pan while it preheated and then mixed dry ingredients in a bag and put aside. I then mixed liquid ingredients in a bowl folded in the pecans added all pecans to the sugar bag, coated them and then spread them out evenly on the buttered pan. Stirred every 15 mins and they came out perfect! The right amount of crunch, sweet/spice and nutty flavor.. a Fall/Holiday go to!!
I made the following changes: add 1 tsp vanilla, add 1/2 tsp cinnamon. Reduce salt to 1/4 tsp and reduce water by 1 tsp . Baked at 275 for 1 hour.

I love this recipe because it is easy, it contains no extra fat, and it's delicious. I've made it every Christmas over the last 4 years and everyone loves it. I have made some changes in the ingredients (the method is the same), however, and I like the outcome better. Here are they are: 1/2 cup sugar (that's plenty!), 2 tsp water + 1 tsp vanilla extract (instead of 1 TBS water), 1/4 tsp. cinnamon (so it doesn't overwhelm the taste of the pecans), and 1/2 tsp salt (same reason as reduction of cinnamon). If you don't want to spray a cookie sheet, use parchment paper instead.

I have made these nuts, using walnuts instead of pecans, several times and absolutely love them. Recipe is easy and best I've tried. I have passed this recipe on to dozens of my friend, who all rave about them, as well. I always double the recipe, mix coated nuts with sugar mixture in a zip lock bag, and bake an additional 15 minutes using a parchment lined cookie sheet. Very little cleanup. After reading the other reviews, I may try substituting the water with vanilla. Sounds interesting. Thanks for sharing. Carolynn Bennett

Super easy, Super delicious and Super impressive given as a gift. The only thing is you MUST stir the nuts every 15 min. otherwise they clump up and don't get that delicious roasted flavor infused throughout the nut. I used almonds that were already roasted and a little salted. I also swapped out vanilla extract for the water. Again I loved this recipe and will make it again and again.

Wonderful recipe. In 2020 our pecan tree gave us a wheelbarrow load of product!! I went by the directions and found the sugar ‘blew out’ the pecan flavor. 
My 2nd batch I reduced the sugar to 1/2 cup, salt and cinnamon by 25%. Adjusted baking times not to burn: Turned out perfect to bring the roasted nut flavor to the front. Thanks so much!!!

I've made them according to the recipe, and have also tried them with a variety of spice combinations. I am going to add a touch of vanilla with the water to the egg white. I am also going to try a sweet and savory batch with a little cayenne added to the sugar, salt, and .cinnamon
An easy way to be a hero with your family and guests! Loved them when my daughter made them and asked for the recipe. Couldn't be happier.
Great!
Easy and short time make. Family favorite ! I gave it on a 1 - 10 scale an eleven!
Quick, easy, and tastes delicious!
Perfect for Christmas offerings to all the neighbors. Pecan halves are always a bargain at Costco for the Holiday season. I could eat these, hand to mouth, all day long, ... and I do.
I added 1/2 t cayenne pepper
I use monk fruit in the raw for zero calories from sweetener. Delicious. I added 1 tsp vanilla to egg mixture. Always well received.
I always add a pinch of allspice. It's very good either way.
